ra.title: NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD: Next Generation Scalable Infrastructure for AI Leadership Reference Architecture Featuring NVIDIA DGX GB200

system.name: DGX GB200 NVL72
system.gpu: NVIDIA B200 Blackwell (2 per GB200 Superchip; 1 Grace CPU per Superchip; 2 Superchips per tray)

compute_nics_per_tray.type: ConnectX-7 single-port OSFP NDR InfiniBand (UG: single port 400G OSFP)

system.dpu_per_tray: 2x BlueField-3 (RA: 2x200Gbps for in-band mgmt + storage; UG: dual-port QSFP each, left port=storagenet, right port=dgxnet; 4 ports total per tray, 2 of 4 per DPU dedicated to storage)
system.bmc: 1x 1GbE RJ45 tray BMC; 2x 1GbE RJ45 BlueField-3 BMC (UG); NVLink switch tray: 1 BMC RJ45 + 2 COMe RJ45 (RA)

su.mgmt_racks: Fig 1: rack row = High Performance Storage | Network Switches | 8x GB200 NVL72 racks | Network Switches | Management Nodes (count of racks not stated; figure is a low-res row photo)

compute_fabric.tech: NVIDIA NDR 400Gb/s InfiniBand, rail-optimized full fat-tree, 4 rails
compute_fabric.oversubscription: non-blocking (full fat-tree); per-SU: 18x400G down per leaf (18 trays) and 2x400G to each of 9 spines (Fig 9)

ethernet_fabric.tech: Spectrum-4 800GbE Ethernet, VXLAN/EVPN segments (storage, in-band, OOB), RoCE for storage; LACP active/active 2x200GbE to DGX trays; eBGP to customer edge
ethernet_fabric.switch_model: NVIDIA SN5600 (leaf/spine/super-spine); SN2201 (1GbE OOB and legacy RJ45 leaf)
ethernet_fabric.mgmt_leaves: 1 pair SN2201 (legacy/RJ45/QSFP uplink devices, in-band 1GbE); OOB SN2201 stack separate
ethernet_fabric.uplinks: Spine->super-spine: 28x800GbE per spine (text), Fig 14 legend '14 x 800 Gbps' (per super-spine group); super-spine switches 4/8/14 for 4/8/16 SUs (2 groups). Leaf->spine 6x800G per leaf, 4x800G per storage/mgmt leaf to spine (Fig 13 legend). Customer edge: >=2x100GbE DR1 (text), 2-4x100GbE BGP (Fig 16). Storage: 16x800Gbps non-blocking per SU; compute side 5:3 blocking.

oob.counts: Not stated in text. Fig 17 shows a stack of ~7 SN2201 OOB switches per SU, 2 SN2201 near racks + 2 SN2201 for IB switches/UFM (Fig 18); each SN2201 uplinks 1x100G to SN5600 spines; racks 1x(2x100G) + 10x1G to rack SN2201 pair. Also 2 TOR mgmt switches per NVL72 rack (UG).

mgmt_plane.ufm: NVIDIA UFM Appliance Enterprise Edition; 2 appliances (C-UFM-1, C-UFM-2) on 1GbE in-band VTEP/OOB
mgmt_plane.nmx: NVIDIA NMX Manager (Fig 16 shows 3 NMX nodes on OOB VTEP); NVLink switches run NVOS
mgmt_plane.bcm_or_mgmt_nodes: Base Command Manager x2 (Fig 16, OOB VTEP); Mission Control software manages SuperPOD; 3x K8s + 2x Slurm head nodes in Fig 16
mgmt_plane.other: Run:ai via Mission Control; NFS user storage 2x100GbE DR1; BMS (building management system) integration via customer edge eBGP

major_components_table.config_size: 18 compute trays x 4 GPUs = 72 GPUs/rack; 9 NVLink switch trays; 8 power shelves

major_components_table.component: Compute trays (derived 8x18; Fig 9 node names GB200-[0001-0144])
major_components_table.config_size: 2 Grace + 4 B200; 4x CX-7; 2x BF3; 4x3.84TB E1.S RAID0 + 1x1.92TB M.2

major_components_table.component: IB spine switches, single SU (Fig 9 labels Spine-01..Spine-09)
Ethernet compute leaf (Fig 13: 4 leaves, each to 2 racks)

cables_table.component: IB compute: tray CX-7 -> rail leaf (derived 144 trays x 4)
IB leaf -> spine (derived 32 leaves x 9 spines x 2)

cables_table.connection: Fig 13: 2x200G per rack-leaf line (gray); text: 4x200GbE per tray
6x800G per compute leaf (Fig 13 legend green); 4x800G storage leaf (brown)

power_cooling.rack_power_kw: ~120 kW per rack (DGX GB200 user guide); SU TDP 1.2 MW (RA)
power_cooling.cdu_or_liquid: Hybrid: GPUs/CPUs direct liquid cooled via rack manifolds and cold plates; other components air cooled. CDU specs not in RA/user guide.
power_cooling.notes: 8 power shelves/rack, each 6x5.5kW PSUs = 33kW (RA says N redundancy, UG says N+N). Shelves convert AC to 50-51V DC to bus bar. Data center should meet Uptime Tier 3 / TIA942-B Rated 3 / EN50600 Class 3.

rack_elevation: RA gives no U-position elevation. Fig 1: one row = High Performance Storage | Network Switches | GB200 NVL72 racks | Network Switches | Management Nodes. Tray U height 1RU (UG); 18 compute + 9 NVLink switch trays + 2 TOR mgmt switches + 8 power shelves in rack.

citations.quote: Each DGX GB200 rack is built with 18 compute trays and 9 NVLink switch trays.
18 compute trays and 9 NVLink switch trays
Each compute tray contains two GB200 Superchips, and each Superchip has two B200 GPUs and one Grace CPU.
There are eight total power shelves in a single DGX GB200 NVL72 rack system.
The compute tray integrates four ConnectX-7 (CX-7) NICs to support InfiniBand NDR (400Gbps)
two BlueFiled-3 (BF3) NICs to support 2x200Gbps connectivity for the In-band Management and Storage networks
18x 1RU compute trays, each with 2 Grace CPUs and 4 Blackwell GPUs.
The rack power consumption is approximately 120kW.
each SU contains 8 DGX GB200 systems
Each SU requires a Thermal Design Power (TDP) of 1.2 Megawatts (MW).
Figure 9 Compute fabric for full 576 GPUs DGX SuperPOD
Each SU contains 4 SLGs to match with the number of IB rails (which equals the number of GPUs per compute tray).
IB Leaf Switch Per SU 32 (Table 3 flattened row: 1152 GPUs, 2 SUs, ... 32 | 64 | 24 | 48)
There are 8 leaf switches (one for each compute rack) and 6 spine switches in each SLG
Spine-01 ... Spine-09 (figure labels only)
NVIDIA Quantum QM9700 InfiniBand switches
figure shows 4 SN5600 leaf switches each connected to 2 racks (figure-only)
Each SU features two SN5600 switches as the aggregation layer or spine layer
One additional pair of SN5600 switches serves as the ingestion point for Storage Appliances and control plane nodes.
One additional pair of SN2201 switches are to connect all legacy devices requiring RJ45 connections or QSFP based uplink connectivity.
Ethernet spines per SU = 2 (Table 4 totals 8/16/32 for 4/8/16 SUs are flattened; derived)
Each Spine is expected to have 28x 800GbE connection uplinks
Each scalable unit is designed to carry 16x 800Gbps non-blocking bandwidth to the storage appliances.
a slightly blocking fabric with a blocking factor of 5:3
NVIDIA SN2201 switch | 48 x 1 Gbps Ethernet switch leveraging copper ports
C-UFM-1 / C-UFM-2 (figure labels)
Single SU aggregate system read | 40 | 125 ... 4 SU aggregate system write | 80 | 250
six 5.5kW PSUs configured as N redundancy and can deliver up to 33kW of power
Each DGX GB200 leverages hybrid cooling with both direct liquid cooling and air cooling

ambiguities: RA is the Nov 2025 'Next Generation Scalable Infrastructure' doc; HTML index <title> still says 'Featuring NVIDIA DGX B200' (copy-paste), body is GB200. No doc_id/version/PDF found on docs.nvidia.com/dgx-superpod/ for GB200 (only GB300 pdf/dgx-spod-gb300-ra.pdf, Vera Rubin, B200/B300 best-practice PDFs).
RA has NO major-components count table, NO cable table, NO U-position rack elevation, NO CDU spec; all counts here beyond text are derived from figures (Figs 9, 13, 16, 17, 18) or multiplication.
Single-SU IB spines: Fig 9 labels Spine-01..Spine-09 (9), but the scale-out SLG design uses 6 spines per SLG (24/SU, Table 3). 1-SU spine count=9 is figure-derived.

Table 1 says 'eight NDR400 connections per system' vs text/UG: 4 CX-7 single-port 400G per tray (4 rails) - the 8 likely counts two trays or is an error (B200 text leftover). Text also refers to 'DGX B200 CPU tray' and 'B200 GPU ... 18 NVL5 links' copy-paste remnants; 'fully tested scales to two SUs' vs architecture page 'four SUs or more contact NVIDIA'; Table 4 (super-spine) flattened and contains stray rows (copy of Table 3 data), super-spine count 4/8/14 for 4/8/16 SUs; super-spine uplinks '28x800GbE' text vs Fig 14 legend '14 x 800 Gbps'.
Switch ports for QM9700 not stated in RA (64 NDR ports/32 OSFP cages is external knowledge); leaf port use 18 down + 18 up inferred from Fig 9.
BF3 speed: RA '2x200Gbps' / '4x 200GbE' per tray; UG says dual-port 400G-capable DPUs; Fig 13 gray link label 2x200G per rack-to-leaf line is unclear (per tray vs per rack).

Power: RA says power shelves 'N redundancy' (6x5.5kW=33kW), UG says N+N; UG ~120 kW rack vs 8x33 kW=264 kW shelf capacity. SU TDP 1.2 MW (RA) vs 8x120=0.96 MW racks, remainder presumably network/storage/mgmt (not stated).
OOB SN2201 count per SU not stated; Fig 17 draws ~7 stacked, Fig 18 draws 2+2+2 groups. Per-rack 2 TOR mgmt switches per UG (model not stated).
Cabling guide (design-guide-cabling-data-centers) is generic NDR/Ethernet cabling, not GB200-specific; no GB200 CDU/rack elevation found there.
Storage tiers are Standard/Enhanced only (mapped to good/better); no 'best' tier.
